narrative: The bridge processed its largest single-day redemption of the tracked period: 51,221 PRL burned (vs 6,078 PRL deposited), pulling custody down 4.65% to 973,523 PRL. The outflow traces to Pearl's own treasury-tagged addresses rather than ordinary user activity — the main lock address barely moved. Custody and the relay's supply endpoint remain in exact agreement, and the surplus/peg reconciliation held (1.04%), so this reads as the bridge correctly processing a large clean redemption, not a fault. Separately, the core repo landed a node-sync hardening fix (witness-commitment validation, reported by mining pool C3Pool; devs confirm consensus/funds were never affected) and yesterday's GPU non-determinism paper kept generating organic follow-up discussion. Network difficulty continues easing (27.2M → 25.7M → 24.9M) with block time holding steady, still reading as post-fork normalization.

Templated pump-signal spam continued at a lower, steadier volume than the mid-week peak. As always, the distinct "Perle Labs" project and unrelated "PRL" usages (Pakistan refinery stock, Physical Review Letters, Polish PRL-era references) are excluded.

sample_tweets.snippet: The federation has three relayers registered on-chain. Day to day, two are actively signing. The 2-of-3 threshold means that gap does not stop a wrap or an unwrap.
Chain congestion changes timing, never the accounting. A busy Ethereum mempool can delay a mint. It cannot make the bridge mint more WPRL than the PRL that is actually locked.
Run the same multiplication on two different NVIDIA GPUs and you can get two different answers. The arithmetic inside is undocumented.
My therapist is gonna hear about this! Green day. $PRL +10.57%

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.
